newsitem.title: USA: Tenn. lottery would raise $302 mln yearly - study.
newsitem.headline: Tenn. lottery would raise $302 mln yearly - study.

text.p: A Tennessee lottery would raise about $302 million a year for college scholarships according to a study released by Sen. Steve Cohen.
Cohen, D-Memphis, is one of the sponsors of a bill that would let voters decide whether to amend the state constitution to permit a lottery.

He released a study by the Tennessee Advisory Commission on Intergovernmental Relations that estimated lottery spending would average $153 per person per year, raising $302 million annually for scholarships.

Tennessee is struggling with a $70 million budget deficit for the year ending June 30. Gov. Don Sundquist has proposed $110 million of cuts for the next fiscal year, including $40 million from higher education.
